bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42534528 (fwupd): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 2 found by fuzz target uswid_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42534528
bug_description.normalized: The staged 25-byte witness is accepted by fwupd as a uSWID container and its trailing 4-byte coSWID payload `bf 0e 0d ff` is handed to the CBOR parser. That payload is an indefinite-length one-pair map whose key byte `0x0e` selects the `version-scheme` field and whose value byte `0x0d` is an embedded one-byte unsigned integer. During `cbor_load`, libcbor reaches that `0x0d` byte through the embedded-uint `callbacks->uint8` path, materializes it as a `cbor_item_t` allocated by `cbor_new_int8()` with `width = CBOR_INT_8` and only one byte of payload storage, and stores that object into the map value slot paired with key `0x0e`. fwupd then dispatches that map entry to `fu_coswid_read_version_scheme`, which checks only that the item is some unsigned integer and immediately calls `cbor_get_uint16(item)`. `cbor_get_uint16` dereferences `*(uint16_t *)item->data`, so it reads two bytes from the one-byte integer object and overruns the heap allocation by one byte. AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` in `cbor_get_uint16`; the fixing patch replaces the width-specific accessor with `cbor_get_int(item)` so the integer is read according to its actual encoded width.

source.description: First project parser statement that consumes the attacker-controlled bytes. It parses the raw 25-byte witness as a uSWID container and materializes header state `st`, which later supplies the payload bounds used to extract the inner coSWID CBOR bytes.
source.value_from: The staged PoC at `gt_results/arvo_42534528/poc` is exactly 25 bytes: `53 42 4f 4d d6 ba 2e ac a3 e6 7a 52 aa ee 3b af 01 15 00 20 20 bf 0e 0d ff`. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` passes those bytes into fwupd's firmware parser; the last four bytes become the coSWID CBOR payload that later reaches the crash.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant state starts when libcbor's uint8 callback handles payload byte `0x0d`. It allocates a one-byte `CBOR_INT_8` object, stores numeric value `13` into that byte, and passes the object into map insertion so it becomes the `pairs[0].value` later misread by fwupd.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `cbor_get_uint16` reads two bytes from `item->data` even though the value object created for the witness was allocated by `cbor_new_int8()` with only one byte of integer storage.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 2` at this line, and the allocation stack points to `cbor_new_int8` in the same file.

root_cause.description: The version-scheme reader enforces only the coarse predicate `cbor_isa_uint(item)` and then unconditionally chooses the 16-bit accessor. It never checks that the decoded CBOR integer actually has `width == CBOR_INT_16`, so one-byte integers still reach `cbor_get_uint16`.
root_cause.note: The patch replaces this line with `(FuCoswidVersionScheme)cbor_get_int(item)`, confirming that the missing obligation is to read the integer according to its actual encoded width rather than assuming a 16-bit payload.

parser_admitted.description: The staged inner payload decodes successfully and passes the root-map check, so fwupd enters the map-walk loop at lines 548-610 where the `version-scheme` branch becomes reachable.

coarse_trace.summary: fwupd parses the outer uSWID header, derives `hdrver = 0x01` and `hdrsz = 0x0015`, and materializes the trailing four bytes `bf 0e 0d ff` as the uncompressed inner coSWID payload because the payload read may short-read at EOF.

libcbor decodes that blob as an indefinite one-pair map: payload byte `0x0e` becomes `pairs[0].key` and flips the map state to expect a value, then payload byte `0x0d` is materialized as a one-byte `CBOR_INT_8` and stored in `pairs[0].value`.

fwupd reads `pairs[0].key` as tag 14 (`VersionScheme`), dispatches that map entry to the version-scheme reader, checks only that the value is some unsigned CBOR integer, and then calls the 16-bit accessor on it.
libcbor dereferences two bytes from the one-byte `cbor_new_int8` allocation backing the map value, producing the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: The first project parser on the vulnerable path consumes the 25-byte witness and materializes uSWID header state `st` from it. That parsed state supplies the header version and payload bounds used to isolate the inner coSWID bytes.

The parsed header version is `0x01` from witness byte 16. It satisfies the minimum-version check at lines 82-88 and later selects the final `else` branch at lines 113-114, which forces `priv->compression = FU_USWID_PAYLOAD_COMPRESSION_NONE`.

fwupd reads the payload window from the parsed header. The witness bytes `15 00` set `hdrsz = 0x0015`, so the inner payload starts at byte offset 21, and `payloadsz` is nonzero, so the `payloadsz == 0x0` rejection is not taken.

fine_trace.code: payload = fu_input_stream_read_bytes(stream, offset + hdrsz, payloadsz, error);
fine_trace.note: Because step 2 selected the uncompressed path, fwupd reads from `offset + hdrsz = 21`. `fu_input_stream_read_bytes` documents and implements that the returned buffer may be smaller than `count`, stopping when `g_input_stream_read` hits EOF, so this 25-byte witness yields exactly the four trailing bytes `bf 0e 0d ff` as `payload` even if `payloadsz` is larger.
When libcbor consumes payload byte `0xbf`, it creates an indefinite root map and pushes it onto the decoder stack with `subitems = 0`, meaning the next appended item will be treated as a map key.

The next payload byte is `0x0e`. `cbor_stream_decode` treats major-type-0 values `0x00` through `0x17` as embedded one-byte unsigned integers, so it dispatches numeric value `14` to the uint8 builder callback.
The key callback materializes that dispatched `14` as a fresh unsigned `cbor_item_t` with `width = CBOR_INT_8` and one byte of payload storage containing `0x0e`.

Because the stack top from step 5 is a map with `subitems == 0`, `_cbor_builder_append` routes step 7's object into `_cbor_map_add_key`, storing it as the first map pair's key slot. For this indefinite map it then toggles `subitems` to `1`, so the next appended item will be treated as that key's value.
The following payload byte is `0x0d`, so libcbor again takes the embedded-uint path and dispatches numeric value `13` to the uint8 builder callback.

The value callback materializes dispatched integer `13` as a fresh unsigned `CBOR_INT_8` object allocated by `cbor_new_int8()`. Its single-byte integer storage contains `0x0d`; this is the heap object later misread by fwupd.

Step 8 left the indefinite map in value-expected state, so `_cbor_builder_append` treats step 10's object as the value for the most recent key and sends it to `_cbor_map_add_value`. After the append, pair 0 is complete and `pairs[0].value` points at this same one-byte integer item.
When fwupd iterates the root map, `fu_coswid_read_tag` consumes `pairs[0].key` from step 8. That key item is an unsigned `CBOR_INT_8` containing `0x0e`, so `tag_id` becomes `14`.

`fu-coswid.rs` enumerates tag 14 as `VersionScheme`, so the `tag_id == FU_COSWID_TAG_VERSION_SCHEME` branch is taken. fwupd therefore passes the completed map value from step 11 as the `item` argument to `fu_coswid_read_version_scheme`.

Root cause. The helper checks only that the incoming map value is some unsigned CBOR integer, which step 11's `CBOR_INT_8` item satisfies, and then unconditionally selects `cbor_get_uint16`. It never checks that the decoded integer width is actually `CBOR_INT_16`.

ASan sink. `cbor_get_uint16` casts step 10's one-byte integer buffer to `uint16_t *` and dereferences two bytes. The saved sanitizer trace reports that this 2-byte read overruns the 49-byte region allocated by `cbor_new_int8`, matching the one-byte payload appended to the `cbor_item_t` header.

format.name: uSWID container with coSWID CBOR payload
format.contract: The verified trigger is the staged 25-byte witness at `gt_results/arvo_42534528/poc`, which fwupd accepts as an uncompressed uSWID blob whose trailing four bytes are `bf 0e 0d ff`. In this witness, key byte `0x0e` selects the `version-scheme` field and value byte `0x0d` decodes through libcbor's embedded-uint path into an unsigned `CBOR_INT_8` map value.
